comments.text: The thing with race cars is, the tyres determine your grip level. cold tyres mean, you have to be extremely careful and conservative with exelaration and breaking, increase throttle slowly and start breaking early and even when your tires are hot, you still have to be extremely careful. you start to slip, you back of the throttle to about half and only increase again, if you regain grip. There is a whole lot of other stuff you need to learn, which can make a race difficult or ruin it, better ask your coach, he can do dedicated training sessions with you about loosing control. If you can't get up to speed, because your tyres are cold or whatever, activate the turn signal, stick to that side of the track and watch your mirrors, the faster traffic has the job to overtake safely. But overall, everyone makes mistakes, it's part of the learning process, the best news is you're alright. GL to your racing career and have fun.

comments.text:
Crashing's a natural learning experience of racing. That said, you shouldn't have been advised to push on cold tyres, so that's someone else's lesson as well as yours. Sorry about your car but I'm glad you walked away relatively unscathed.

Edit: Video title change to "I survived my car crash" is needlessly sensationalist and clickbaity. You had the most innocuous crash health wise by simply losing control and ran off track then glanced alongside the barrier. comments.text:
🔥🔥🔥 🙌 Ciao! It’s good to see you doing this type of stuff. The livery and helmet are very well thought, fitting with your job and channel! (And the car obviously is amazing) The crash was really unexpected haha, hopefully the car is not going to be too much of a hassle to fix (spoiler: it does get expensive!). Once you get it ready you should practice a lot since the crash was very avoidable. It’s normal at the start to crash many times but it’s important to be careful cause even with modern safety standards a high speed mistake can hurt (especially wrists and back/neck). After all it takes practice cause those race cars drive more aggressively than the road cars so you must be really smooth with the throttle and steering (traction control didn’t save you). 

By the way since I see you’re really passionate about racing (and specifically Ferrari), once you get confident in these kind of cars I really suggest you try getting into Ferrari’s XX Programme. The Ferrari XX programme is is pretty much the final goal. It is absolutely incredible and it doesn’t get any crazier. It’s not only the driving but also everything that’s around it, the luxury, the cars, driver events (in Italy they literally line up all of the cars and drivers on the track and have them rev and have jets and helicopters fly over them), and they bring the car for you around tracks all over the world. You should get a little more confident in the 296 first though cause the Ferraris of the XX programme are on a whole different level (have a look if you haven’t seen them running). In my opinion the FXX K EVO is the car you should get if one day you choose to do this. It’s incredibly loud and the feeling inside is crazy, the engine screaming + the wind and also the speed of the car can exceed 370km/h (230mph). Also not to mention it’s a V12, so double the cylinders, and it’s equipped with F1 technology. A mistake with that car though is really dangerous and expensive, so you must get confident with a wide range of track cars before pushing it. The programme is also amazing for networking and connections (given it’s exclusiveness) and you have contact with F1 drivers as well as massive companies, sponsors, and billionaires, which could be really useful given your huge channel. (For some reason this paragraph sounded like an ad hahaha)

Anyways as an Italian it’s really nice to see you appreciate racing and the Motorsport world, and well done on achieving this so young! Again congratulations on the beautiful car and I wish you the best, good luck in future practice sessions!
